definitions: A time-frequency spectral localization technique that provides a frequency-dependent resolution, combining features of the Short-Time Fourier Transform and the wavelet transform.
An invertible transform that maps a time-domain signal to a two-dimensional time-frequency representation, often used in signal processing for analyzing non-stationary signals.
examples: The Stockwell Transform was applied to seismic data.
Analysis of the Stockwell Transform revealed transient features.
The Stockwell Transform offers advantages over traditional Fourier methods.
